images.title: 4 and 6 share a 2, 8 and 3 share nothing
images.purpose: Compares factor tiles: 4 and 6 overlap on one 2 and only cover 12, while 8 and 3 share nothing and cover all of 24.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two Venn diagrams side by side, a before and after comparison.
images.exact_structure: Left Venn: two overlapping circles labelled 4 and 6. The 4 circle holds one tile 2 in its own part; the overlap holds one tile 2; the 6 circle holds one tile 3 in its own part. Under it: LCM 12, in an amber (#E69F00) tag. Right Venn: two separate circles labelled 8 and 3. The 8 circle holds three tiles 2; the 3 circle holds one tile 3. Under it: LCM 24, in a green (#009E73) tag. All tiles are small teal (#0072B2) squares with white numerals. Exactly 4 tiles on the left, 4 on the right. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Tests for 4 and 6 only prove divisibility by 12; tests for 3 and 8 prove divisibility by 24.

image_decisions.why: Overlapping factor tiles show why the shared 2 makes 4 and 6 fail as a test for 24.
